analysis.title: Mirion Technologies Inc. (MIR): 3Q26 First Take: EBITDA miss, orders robust, organic growth positive
key_insights: MIR reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $64.8mn versus GS estimate of $68.1mn and FactSet $68.3mn, driven by weaker Nuclear & Safety margins (25.7% vs GS 27.8%), partly offset by Medical (37.8% vs GS 36.7%). GS attributes the shortfall to Paragon acquisition dilution and mix.
Organic sales growth was +6.5% versus GS +6.0%. Nuclear & Safety grew +6.3% (GS +5.5%), helped by Nuclear Power +14% y/y. Medical grew +6.7% (GS +7.0%).
Orders rose +62% organically, with Nuclear Power orders +105%. Backlog grew +10% sequentially to $1.25bn, and about 59% of it is expected to be recognized in 4Q26 and 2027.
$140mn of large opportunities were awarded in 3Q (vs $51mn in 2Q). Management expects another ~$125mn in the pipeline for Q4.

MIR lowered its 2026 adj. EBITDA guide to $285-$292mn (from $285-$300mn), against GS and consensus of $290mn each. It narrowed adj. EPS guidance to $0.50-$0.54 (from $0.48-$0.55), against GS and consensus of $0.55 each.
Adjusted FCF guidance was raised to $170-$185mn from $155-$175mn.

GS says it is encouraged by organic growth and order strength, but expects the EBITDA miss and lowered guide to weigh on the stock the next day. GS keeps a Buy rating with a $20 12-month price target, based on 18.0x its Q5-Q8 EBITDA forecast.
Total 3Q26 revenue was $277.8mn versus GS $272.1mn and FactSet $275.4mn, up 24.5% y/y. Cash EPS was $0.12, in line with GS and FactSet.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Buy and a $20 PT (18.0x Q5-Q8 EBITDA) after the 3Q26 print. Organic growth and orders were strong, but the EBITDA miss and lower guide are expected to pressure the stock. The PT was cut from $23 on 29-Jul-26 and from $20 to $20 on 30-Sep-26 per the history table.
